title: Unit 1: Study Skills - Key Vocabulary & Terminology
content:
📌 Transient (Adjective)
• English: Lasting for a very short time; temporary.
• Amharic: ጊዜያዊ፣ አላፊ
• Synonyms: Temporary, Fleeting
• Antonyms: Permanent, Lasting
• Example: Spoken language is transient, so taking notes during a lecture is essential.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Distractions (Noun)
• English: Things that prevent someone from giving full attention.
• Amharic: ትኩረት የሚስቡ/የሚያበላሹ ነገሮች
• Synonyms: Interruptions, Disturbances
• Antonyms: Focus, Concentration
• Example: Sit near the front of the room to avoid environmental distractions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Verbatim (Adverb / Adjective)
• English: In exactly the same words as were used originally.
• Amharic: ቃል በቃል
• Synonyms: Word-for-word, Exactly
• Antonyms: Paraphrased, Summarized
• Example: Do not try to write down the lecture verbatim; focus on main ideas.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Cues (Noun)
• English: Signals or hints given by a speaker to indicate key points.
• Amharic: ጠቋሚ ምልክቶች
• Synonyms: Signals, Hints, Indicators
• Antonyms: Misdirections, Distractions
• Example: Good students listen for vocal cues from the lecturer to identify important topics.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Discriminating (Adjective)
• English: Having or showing refined judgment; selective.
• Amharic: መምረጥ የሚያውቅ፣ ለይቶ አዋቂ
• Synonyms: Selective, Perceptive
• Antonyms: Indiscriminate, Careless
• Example: Effective note-taking requires being a discriminating listener.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Invaluable (Adjective)
• English: Extremely useful; priceless.
• Amharic: እጅግ ጠቃሚ፣ ዋጋ የማይተመንለት
• Synonyms: Priceless, Crucial
• Antonyms: Worthless, Useless
• Example: Reading provides invaluable knowledge for your future career.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Skim (Verb)
• English: Read quickly to get the general idea or gist.
• Amharic: አጠቃላይ ሐሳቡን ለማግኘት በፍጥነት ማንበብ
• Synonyms: Glance through, Scan roughly
• Antonyms: Read thoroughly, Scrutinize
• Example: I skimmed through the chapter to understand the main topic before class.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Scan (Verb)
• English: Look through text quickly to locate a specific piece of information.
• Amharic: የተወሰነ መረጃ/ቃል በፍጥነት መፈለግ
• Synonyms: Search, Browse
• Antonyms: Ignore, Overlook
• Example: Scan the table of contents to find where the vocabulary section is located.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Assimilate (Verb)
• English: Take in and fully understand information or ideas.
• Amharic: መቀበል፣ መረዳት፣ መዋሃድ
• Synonyms: Absorb, Comprehend
• Antonyms: Misunderstand, Reject
• Example: Students read academic books to assimilate new concepts into their understanding.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Repertoire (Noun)
• English: A stock of skills, techniques, or devices used in a particular field.
• Amharic: የተካኑባቸው ክህሎቶች/ልምዶች ስብስብ
• Synonyms: Collection, Stock, Range
• Antonyms: Limitation, Inability
• Example: University students should use their entire repertoire of reading skills.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Cursory (Adjective)
• English: Hasty and therefore not thorough or detailed.
• Amharic: ላዩን ብቻ የሆነ፣ ፈጣን ምልከታ
• Synonyms: Superficial, Hasty
• Antonyms: Thorough, Detailed
• Example: A newspaper often gives only a cursory coverage of complex events.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 At their disposal (Idiom / Phrase)
• English: Available for one's use whenever desired.
• Amharic: በእጃቸው ላይ ያለ፣ ለመጠቀም የተዘጋጀ
• Synonyms: Available, Ready for use
• Antonyms: Unavailable, Restricted
• Example: Students have various learning strategies at their disposal.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Keys (Noun)
• English: Essential tools or crucial factors that provide access to understanding.
• Amharic: ዋና ቁልፎች፣ ወሳኝ መሳሪያዎች
• Synonyms: Essentials, Secrets, Solutions
• Antonyms: Obstacles, Barriers
• Example: Reading skills are the keys to unlocking complex academic knowledge.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Access (Noun / Verb)
• English: The opportunity or means to enter, approach, or retrieve information.
• Amharic: ማግኘት፣ የመጠቀም ዕድል
• Synonyms: Entry, Admission, Availability
• Antonyms: Restriction, Limitation
• Example: Students need easy access to diverse library reference materials.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Perceptions (Noun)
• English: The ways in which something is regarded, understood, or interpreted.
• Amharic: ግንዛቤዎች፣ አመለካከቶች
• Synonyms: Views, Insights, Attitudes
• Antonyms: Misunderstandings, Misconceptions
• Example: Academic reading helps broaden a student's perceptions of world issues.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Interpreted (Verb)
• English: Explained, understood, or analyzed in a specified way.
• Amharic: ተተረጎመ፣ ትርጉም ተሰጠው
• Synonyms: Understood, Analyzed, Clarified
• Antonyms: Misconstrued, Misunderstood
• Example: The survey results were interpreted using statistical analysis.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Glancing through (Phrasal Verb)
• English: Looking at or reading something very quickly without paying attention to detail.
• Amharic: ላዩን መመልከት፣ በፍጥነት ማየት
• Synonyms: Browsing, Skimming, Flipping through
• Antonyms: Studying, Scrutinizing
• Example: He was glancing through the daily paper while waiting for the lecture.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Extract (Verb)
• English: To remove, derive, or select specific facts or main points from a text.
• Amharic: መቀነስ፣ መረጃ መዞር/ማውጣት
• Synonyms: Obtain, Withdraw, Gather
• Antonyms: Insert, Add
• Example: Effective note-takers extract only the essential points from the presentation.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Vary (Verb)
• English: To change or differ according to the circumstances or purpose.
• Amharic: መለያየት፣ መለዋወጥ
• Synonyms: Differ, Alter, Fluctuate
• Antonyms: Remain constant, Stay same
• Example: Your reading speed should vary based on the difficulty of the passage.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Themes (Noun)
• English: The main ideas, subjects, or underlying topics in a text or lecture.
• Amharic: ዋና ዋና ርዕሰ ጉዳዮች/ሀሳቦች
• Synonyms: Topics, Subject matters, Core ideas
• Antonyms: Details, Minor facts
• Example: The professor outlined the central themes of the course during the orientation.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Recognizing (Verb)
• English: Identifying or acknowledging words, concepts, or details previously learned.
• Amharic: መለየት፣ ማወቅ
• Synonyms: Identifying, Perceiving
• Antonyms: Ignoring, Overlooking
• Example: Reading is about understanding context, not just recognizing individual words.
